- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model tends to overpredict; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction.
- After a sharp price spike (true outcome > 70), model often overshoots in the following days; cap forecast at +5–10% above peak or use lagged mean reversion.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if sentiment is mixed or neutral, apply a 1–2% upward bias to account for lingering momentum.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33), model often fails to adjust quickly; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days or apply a downward correction of 2–5%.
- In low-sentiment periods (sentiment ≤ 0.33), model tends to overfit recent noise; use 3–5 day moving average or ignore short-term volatility in forecast.
